title: Claiborne William's brass band and early jazz dances
summary: The first music he heard was Claiborne William's 15-piece brass band parading, then a seven-piece version playing fox trots, rags and what was then called jazz at dances.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: The first kind of music I heard when I was a boy at home to remember, that was brass band music. Professor Claiborne William brass band. Oh yeah, I've heard of the band from Donaldsonville. Professor Claiborne William brass band used to come to Napoleonville and play parades. Well I was around about eight years old. I used to come there and play parades with you and uh, uh, Donaldsonville is just about 16 miles from the coast. That's old.
Uh, did you hear any uh dance music? Uh, and how, first of all let's get back to the parade though, did the band sort of swing like they do in the street today? No, no, it wasn't nothing like that.
No, there wasn't. Um, they only played uh, these marches, regular marches that they had in their little red books.
Like the Sousa marches and things of that type. That's all they was playing then. And then uh,

uh, the band would come to town on Sunday evening and do a parade, parade for the Archfellas and that night the Archfellas will have a dance. Uh, well at that time Claiborne William had a 15-piece brass band.
Yeah, I never did hear much about that brass band. I've talked to a lot of people about him,

but I never thought about the brass band. Yeah, a 15-piece brass band. Then he, for the dance that night, he would break the band down to seven pieces. And, well in fact that was the first swing band I was, Claiborne William. I was a kid. I used to go in the dance hall and just sit around the bandstand and listen.
Yeah. Um, what type of music was it in those days? Can you remember, regular, well like Foxtrots or One Steps or Walls?

Yeah. They were playing Foxtrots. They were playing Foxtrots. And they had what you call a one step dance they'll play. Then they had a couple of rags they'll play. Yeah. Something like ragtime music. And at that time they was playing Dixieland, but they wasn't calling it exactly Dixieland at that time. Yeah, I know. They were playing the same thing, practically the same thing the Dixieland is playing now. But they wasn't calling it Dixieland at that time. They was calling it uh, jazz. Yeah. Calling it jazz. Well, they played jazz in the dance halls and in the street they played these regular marches out of the books.
